summary: Pilot Peak Lookout in the Payette National Forest began as a 1919 log cabin, gained its L-4 cab in 1954, and was listed on the NHLR in 2020.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 10-foot concrete base

events.note: 12x12-foot log cabin on the ground; first structure on the site.
New L-4 structure on a 10-foot block with an enclosed tower; the current lookout.
Known staff listed for 1974-1975 by Idaho Fire Lookouts.
Savage Creek fire; lookout ordered evacuated after the fire jumped Elk Creek.
Caroline Huntley listed as staff for 2010-2011 (Idaho Fire Lookouts). Keeping Watch dates the Huntleys' lookout work to the early and mid-2000s.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, October 3, 2020.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Keeping Watch gives 1919; NHLR and firelookout.com date the 1919 log cabin and the 1954 L-4 cab separately. The story reports both dates.
Keeping Watch ties Jim and Caroline Huntley to lookout work in the early and mid-2000s; Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Caroline Huntley at this tower for 2010-2011. Both are reported without choosing one.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 3.0 matches only the 10-foot base in the sources, not a confirmed total height, so it is left out of facts. Elevation: NHLR says 8,075 ft (2,461 m), firelookout.com says 8057 ft; the brief's 2461.3 m follows NHLR. Access level is not stated by any source, so access is omitted; visit.drive_up comes from the Idaho Fire Lookouts 'Drive-Up Staffed' label. Keeping Watch says L-4 cabs were built until 1952, which is earlier than the 1954 L-4 here; the design label may be loose. The Weebly list page has a '1932 log lookout house' entry that is not clearly this tower (the page lists many Pilot Peaks), so it is not used. A separate Idaho Fire Lookouts Pilot Peak in southern Idaho (1932 L-4, NHLR 2011) is a different tower. A 2020 Idaho County Free Press article on restoration appeared in search results but returned HTTP 429 on fetch, so restoration is not in the story; worth a retry.
